$comment: CC:Tweaked HTTP lockdown, applied by itzg's PATCH_DEFINITIONS at every container start.
WHY THIS IS A PATCH AND NOT A COMMITTED CONFIG FILE:
CC:Tweaked's HTTP rules live in the SERVER config, which Forge stores per-world at
world/serverconfig/computercraft-server.toml. Both data/config/ and data/world/ are
gitignored on purpose (see .gitignore: tracking files the server rewrites leaves the
droplet worktree permanently dirty and blocks git pull --ff-only in gitops/deploy.sh).
So the config cannot be committed. Patching it at startup is the mechanism that
survives that constraint and re-asserts itself on every boot.
WHAT THIS CLOSES:
Children write and run arbitrary Lua on this server. With CC:Tweaked's default rules
(deny $private, allow *), any player could make the SERVER issue outbound HTTP to any
host on the internet. That is server-side request forgery with a child at the keyboard,
and it is reachable today by anyone already whitelisted.
RULE ORDER MATTERS: CC:Tweaked evaluates http.rules top to bottom, first match wins.
The private-range denies come first, then the catch-all deny. $private already covers
loopback, RFC1918 and link-local; the explicit CIDRs are kept as belt-and-braces in
case $private is unsupported on a future version, and because 169.254.169.254 is the
cloud metadata endpoint on this DigitalOcean droplet and deserves to be named.
FUNCTIONAL TRADEOFF, ACCEPTED DELIBERATELY: the built-in pastebin and wget programs
now fail with 'domain not permitted' for every host. To allow one host back, insert a
single {host, action: allow} entry ABOVE the catch-all deny. That is also how the
Instructor Terminal gets its one allowed origin (see minecraft_website issue #36).
http.enabled stays TRUE on purpose: the API remains present so a denied request
returns a clear 'domain not permitted' error a child can understand, rather than the
confusing 'http is disabled' that comes from switching the whole API off.
